about.body: The OM611 is a 2.1/2.2-litre inline-four diesel engine produced by Mercedes-Benz from 1995 to 2006. It was a key engine in the commercial vehicle range, powering a wide variety of Sprinter vans, Vario minibuses, and the first-generation Vito panel van. It was also used in the Mercedes-Benz V-Class (W638) as the 2.2 CDI. The engine is known for its robust design, but like all diesel engines of its era, it is susceptible to injector seal wear and EGR clogging over time and mileage.

byModel.body: In the Sprinter, the OM611 was fitted to the T1N generation across the 208, 211, and 212 model designations, covering the full range of panel vans, crew vans, and chassis cabs. In the Vario, the OM611 appeared in the W670 generation in 508D, 510D, and 512D models — these were the larger minibuses and panel vans, typically used for commercial passenger transport.
